stories.description: Ousmane Dembélé, Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappé are among the top contenders for the men’s Ballon d’Or. The 30 men’s and 30 women’s nominees were revealed by France Football magazine on Tuesday, with the winners to be announced at a ceremony in London on October 26.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Hormuz impasse deepens: Iran retaliates against US targets after its oil tankers destroyed
stories.description: Iran launched fresh attacks against US targets in the Middle East on Wednesday in retaliation for American strikes on Iranian oil tankers, dragging the foes deeper into war. Tehran's powerful Revolutionary Guards said Wednesday they attacked 20 US vessels trying to pass through the Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway for the world's oil and gas that Iran has largely controlled since the war erupted. The United States and Iran are locked in a stalemate six months into the war, with Iran maintaining a stranglehold on the Strait of Hormuz and Washington pushing a campaign to choke Iran's ports and economy.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: JNIM jihadists step up incursions into northern Benin
stories.description: Al Qaeda affiliate JNIM has been intensifying its activities in Benin since 2022. The country serves as a transit corridor between the areas of operation of the group, which is well established in Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso. Two nature reserves have become logistical hubs for the jihadist fighters. Benin's army is striving to hold the line.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Russian drone strike near Ukraine-Moldova border kills at least two as Ukraine targets oil terminal
stories.description: An overnight Russian drone strike at a border crossing between Ukraine and Moldova killed at least two people, Odesa's regional governor said Wednesday. Moldovan Prime Minister Vasile Tofan said that 17 drones had hit Moldovan territory in August alone as both Kyiv and Moscow ramp up long-range strikes on military and energy infrastructure.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: European space sector in the spotlight as Paris hosts International Space Summit
stories.description: Paris's Grand Palais will host a two-day International Space Summit this Wednesday to promote global cooperation in the sector. A number of deals and investments for European space firms are expected to be announced as part of a wider plan to strengthen Europe's position in a field dominated by the US and China. Also in this edition: the US and Canada are locked in a tit-for-tat battle over tariffs.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: Why is France so good at animation?
stories.description: 🇫🇷 🎞️ Usually associated with high fashion and culinary excellence, the French touch is prominent in another field not many know about: animation. The French animation industry is the third-largest exporter of animated content in the world, behind only the US and Japan. But why is France so good at animation? FRANCE 24's Tanishk Saha explains.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: OpenAI says its models solved one of math's hardest problems as researchers cry foul
stories.description: US tech giant OpenAI on Tuesday said it had solved one of the hardest problems in mathematics with an unreleased artificial intelligence model after just 88 hours – and millions of dollars' worth of computing power. But a US mathematician and a researcher at rival Anthropic allege that OpenAI only took up the problem after it had gotten wind of their own AI-assisted efforts to crack the challenge which had demanded months to craft a radically distinctive approach.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Eiffel Tower row over Hindu sect BAPS unites French politicians – but divides Indian diaspora
stories.description: France got a crash course on the Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha (BAPS), a Hindu sect at the heart of an Eiffel Tower strike this week. But for Indians in France who have been trying to raise awareness of far-right Hindu groups, it comes too late. As the 2027 election campaign goes into high gear, some fear the issue will be politicised by the French far right.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Rubio hails Colombia's new pro-Trump leader De la Espriella on first stop of Latin American tour
stories.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio pledged closer security cooperation with Bogota on the first stop of his three-nation tour of pro-Washington Latin American nations. Rubio hailed the election of Colombian President Abelardo De La Espriella as part of a growing alignment with US interests across the Western Hemisphere.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Champions League: Madrid and Mbappé defeat Inter despite defensive lapses
stories.description: Real Madrid won the headline clash of the first night of the Champions League against Inter Milan (2-1). Kylian Mbappé, who opened the scoring, is now the fifth-highest goalscorer in the competition’s history.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Travellers in UK face ongoing disruption after air traffic control glitch
stories.description: Flights from British airports began to resume Wednesday after a glitch in the country's air traffic control service left hundreds of thousands of passengers stranded. Authorities warned that travellers would continue to experience delays as airlines scrambled to recover from the outage.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: US bans Canadian alcohol, motorcycles and dairy products as trade spat escalates
stories.description: The US and Canada escalated a bitter trade dispute on Tuesday, with Washington imposing new import bans on Canadian alcohol, motorcycles and dairy products as Ottawa's retaliatory tariffs on US goods took effect.
stories.subject: Business

stories.title: Key post-9/11 air toxicity information was kept secret for 25 years
stories.description: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani released tens of thousands of previously undisclosed documents on Tuesday detailing what city officials knew about toxic air after the September 11 attacks, as the 25th anniversary approaches and thousands continue to suffer from related illnesses.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Smithsonian chief Lonnie Bunch steps down amid Trump administration pressure
stories.description: The Smithsonian announced Tuesday that Secretary Lonnie Bunch will leave his post at the end of the year, as the institution faces continued scrutiny from the Trump administration over how its museums present US history.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Middle East live: US destroys five Iranian oil tankers as Iran threatens Kuwait and Bahrain
stories.description: US forces destroyed five Iranian oil carriers on Tuesday after Tehran launched ballistic missiles at an American warship twice in recent days. Iran also launched strikes on US targets in Jordan, and threatened attacks on oil tankers off Kuwait and Bahrain. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: ‘Was this a state visit?’ Indian opposition leader raises serious questions over Paris BAPS temple
stories.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome Anish Gawande. He sees the controversy surrounding the inauguration of the BAPS temple near Paris as more than an isolated dispute over the treatment of female staff at the Eiffel Tower. From his perspective, the incident exposes a broader and insufficiently scrutinized intersection of religion, diplomacy, political power, labor practices, and diaspora politics. At the center of his argument is an ambiguity over the boundary between private religious and state-sanctioned activity.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Mourinho's Real Madrid edge Inter Milan in Champions League opener
stories.description: Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid began their Champions League campaign with a 2-1 win over his former side Inter Milan on Tuesday, taking a two-goal lead before Carlos Augusto pulled one back. Thibaut Courtois and Inter goalkeeper Josep Martinez both made crucial saves as Madrid held on for victory at the Santiago Bernabeu.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: UK, France, ⁠Canada sanction Israeli West Bank goods
stories.description: Israel said on Tuesday it was closing Britain's consulate in East Jerusalem in response to plans by the UK, France and Canada to block imports from Israeli settlements in the West Bank. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Julie Norman, Associate Fellow with the Middle East and North Africa Programme at Chatham House and Director of UCL’s Israel-Palestine Initiative.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Accelerating diversification: Canada seeks economic sovereignty amid Trump's 'nonsensical' posturing
stories.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome Jean Simard, President and CEO of the Aluminum Association of Canada. According to Simard, the US-Canada aluminum dispute is not your conventional disagreement over trade, but rather a 'Trump posture that makes no sense". As American industrial demand substantially exceeds domestic production capacity, tariffs will do nothing to reduce Canadian aluminum from the US market. Protectionism does not eliminate interdependence, explains Simard, it makes that interdependence considerably more expensive.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: Kenya cracks down on foreign traders
stories.description: In tonight's edition, Hundreds of Burundians flocked to ⁠their embassy in ​Nairobi to get travel documents to return home. Also, in his first speech to the National assembly, Senegal’s Prime Minister Ahmadou Al Aminou Lo slams the rise of xenophobic rhetoric on the continent. And I speak to the founder of an AI surgical non-profit of the work being done in Tanzania to extend the reach of the country's 27 over burdened neurosurgeons.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Paris probes why women staff removed from Eiffel Tower for Hindu visit
stories.description: The mayor of Paris on Tuesday ordered investigations over the removal of women staff at the Eiffel Tower during a visit by a Hindu religious group which prompted an employee walkout and the one-day closure of the monument. The Eiffel Tower, which says it receives nearly seven million people a year, reopened on Tuesday morning after a furore resulted in the landmark being shut down on Monday. FRANCE 24's Monte Francis reports
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: Canada PM stands his ground as Ottawa's retaliatory tariffs on US goods take effect
stories.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said it was a shame that trade talks with the US collapsed but that he would continue to fight to protect Canada's sovereignty, as his government's promised counter-tariffs on $20 billion worth of US exports took effect. Also in the segment, Cuba says economic damage from decades of US trade embargo has risen to a record $8 billion.
stories.subject: Business

stories.title: Trump posts AI map showing US 'takeover' of North America, Iceland and Caribbean
stories.description: Donald Trump shared an AI-generated map Monday appearing to show the US absorbing Canada, Mexico, Greenland, Iceland, Cuba and parts of the Caribbean into a giant “United States of America”. Shared with no context, the post sparked diplomatic backlash with Iceland summoning its ambassador and Mexico reiterating its sovereignty. Denmark also pushed back over Greenland. Online, the map has triggered widespread ridicule and questions about Trump’s fitness for office.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 'Europe's museums are under siege', art recovery expert says
stories.description: Two thieves sliced through a fence, climbed through a window and stole four valuable Renoir paintings Tuesday from a small museum on the French Riviera, but abandoned two of the artworks as they fled, authorities said. FRANCE 24's Mark Owen speaks with Christopher Marinello, a lawyer and founder of Art Recovery International. He says that offering a reward for information could go a long way in recovering stolen artworks.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Canada will move faster from US reliance as tariffs take effect and Trump response looms
stories.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Tuesday that Canada would move faster to reduce its economic reliance on the United States as retaliatory tariffs took effect on about $20 billion worth of U.S. goods and the country braced for President Donald Trump’s response. FRANCE 24's Christopher Guly reports from Ottawa.
stories.subject: Business

stories.title: Trump tells Putin he wants swift end to Ukraine war, Kremlin says
stories.description: US President Donald Trump told Russian President Vladimir Putin he wanted a swift end to the Ukraine war, the Kremlin said, arguing that peace could pave the way for a broad restoration of US-Russia ties. The hour-long call Tuesday followed weekend talks by US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in Moscow and Kyiv to try to revive stalled peace efforts.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: French police hunt Renoir thieves after lightning museum heist
stories.description: French police on Tuesday hunted for two thieves who escaped with two Renoir paintings from a museum, after abandoning two others as they fled, in a burglary that reignited concerns about the protection of France's cultural heritage. The heist is the latest in a string of such robberies including the daylight theft last year of crown jewellery valued at around $100 million from the Louvre in Paris. FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Netanyahu under fire over report UAE warned of October 7 attack
stories.description: Israeli opposition leaders on Tuesday called Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu unfit to serve after a report that the United Arab Emirates had warned him before the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack. Haaretz newspaper, in a report excerpted from a forthcoming book by its reporters, said UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan spoke to Netanyahu a week and a half before the attack and told him that Hamas was planning a major operation. FRANCE 24's Monte Francis reports.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: UK, France, Canada to ban imports from Israeli settlements
stories.description: Britain, France and Canada said Tuesday they will ban imports from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, with a UK minister accusing Israel of turning a blind eye to the "ethnic cleansing" of Palestinians there. FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell reports.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Missiles or mediation? Trump envoys shuttle between Russia and Ukraine
stories.description: Exactly two months ago, Ukraine’s momentum was all the talk at a Nato summit in Turkey. What with its long-range drones and Donald Trump’s surprise announcement that the US would allow Kyiv to produce Patriot anti-ballistic missiles on home soil. That was then. This is now: Trump's deal's yet to materialize, Russia’s ramped up cruise missile launches and Ukraine’s run out of air defenses to stop them. Moscow's also failing to stop incoming missiles. What happens in war when for both sides, offense proves better than defense?
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Messi, Mbappé and Kane headline Ballon d'Or shortlist, Vozinha named for Yashin award
stories.description: Eight-time laureate Lionel Messi is in the 30-man shortlist for the 2026 Men's Ballon ​d'Or, with Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappé among the favourites to succeed France's Ousmane Dembélé. Cape Verde's Vozinha has been shortlisted for the goalkeepers' Yashin Trophy after his heroics at the recent World Cup.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 'US Midterm elections tend to be referendums on the unpopularity of the president'
stories.description: Annette Young is pleased to welcome Michelle Swers, Professor of Government at Georgetown University. She frames the New Hampshire primary as both a major Senate contest and an unusually strong indication of the national political climate ahead of November. While Democrats face a difficult Senate map and cannot afford to surrender an open seat they already hold, the broader midterm political environment might become a referendum on President Donald Trump’s performance. New Hampshire is particularly instructive because its closely divided electorate makes national political currents more visible. Swers argues that Trump’s low approval and the local economic consequences of tariffs on Canada create significant headwinds for Republicans, especially in a state whose political identity is strongly associated with resistance to taxation.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: US war on Iran: 'Incompetent administration when it comes to negotiations and prosecuting war'
stories.description: Mark Owen is pleased to welcome Barbara Slavin, Distinguished Fellow at the Simpson Center. She frames the war in the Persian Gulf as a mutually damaging stalemate in which neither Washington nor Tehran has found a politically sustainable exit: "There are no winners in this war". Her central argument is that the conflict has created a problem of face-saving as much as military strategy. The US faces rising economic and electoral costs, while Iran confronts shortages, inflation, domestic dissent and intensified repression. Neither side, in her assessment, can plausibly claim success.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: The 'Brenaissance': Brendan Fraser on 'Pressure', winning an Oscar in 'The Whale' and 'The Mummy 4'
stories.description: From "The Mummy" to his Oscar-winning performance in "The Whale", Brendan Fraser's career has taken some extraordinary turns. At the Deauville American Film Festival, he talks to Eve Jackson about his "Brenaissance", playing General Dwight D. Eisenhower in "Pressure", what D-Day can teach us about the dangers of ignoring science and his return as Rick O'Connell in "The Mummy 4".
stories.subject: Science

stories.title: World Cup final scorer Torres leads Ballon d'Or nominees
stories.description: Ferran Torres, whose goal against Argentina won the World Cup for Spain in July, leads a 30-man list for the men's Ballon d'Or revealed on Tuesday.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Eiffel Tower reopens after row over limits on women staff
stories.description: The Eiffel Tower reopened Tuesday, a day after one of the world's most-visited landmarks was closed by a strike to protest what a union official called "unacceptable" management instructions limiting the presence of women during a visit by a Hindu religious group close to Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling nationalist party.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Middle East live: Israel to close British consulate in Jerusalem after sanctions on settlements
stories.description: British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband accused the Israeli government on Tuesday of turning a "blind eye" to what he called "ethnic cleansing" by settlers in the West Bank as the UK joined France and ten other countries in banning imports from Israeli settlements in the occupied territory. The decision comes amid rising violence over settlement expansion. Follow our liveblog for the latest.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: France joins ban on products from Israeli settlements in West Bank
stories.description: France will join the UK and other countries in launching a process to ban products from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, Foreign Minister Jean-Noël ​Barrot said on Tuesday, amid rising settler violence that has further undermined prospects for a two-state solution with the Palestinians. France 24's Marc Perelman has the details.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: UK ban on goods from Israeli settlements 'evidence of Netanyahu's failure'
stories.description: British foreign minister Ed Miliband accused the Israeli government on Tuesday of turning a "blind eye" to what he called "ethnic cleansing" by settlers in the West Bank. Miliband told parliament the UK government would introduce "an import ban on goods from illegal settlements in the occupied territories", in a move coordinated with other countries. Jordana Miller, ABC correspondent in Jerusalem, told France 24 that the ban was evidence of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to rein in the far-right elements of his government that has facilitated the growth of settlements.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 🔴Israel to shut down UK consulate in Jerusalem in response to sanctions on settlements
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Eiffel Tower reopens after row over removing women staff
stories.description: The Eiffel Tower reopened on Tuesday after staff walked out over the removal of women colleagues during a visit by a Hindu religious group which later apologised. The operating company that runs the Paris landmark, SETE, acknowledged that the Hindu delegation had requested the visit on Saturday be organised so as to limit "interactions with women" and said that "these conditions should not have been accepted".
stories.subject: Business

stories.title: Sounding the fire alarm: Why French firefighters are going on strike
stories.description: We dive into the particularities of France's firefighting system, including how they came to be called "sapeurs-pompiers", this as firefighters kick off six weeks of strikes. Finally, we discuss how other public service workers are also calling for industrial action.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Spoiler alert: AI in cinema 'just a tool, won’t replace actors and human beings'
stories.description: Eve Irvine is pleased to welcome film producer Lahoucine Grimich. He challenges the prevailing narrative that cinema is an industry in existential crisis. While acknowledging that viewing habits have dramatically shifted since the pandemic, he argues that streaming platforms, public support and theatrical exhibition are not competing forces. As demonstrated in the French model, they form parts of an interconnected financing ecosystem in which cinema can adapt without ever abandoning the big screen. He frames filmmaking as a form of cultural sovereignty: societies need films not simply as entertainment, but to recognise themselves and to create what he calls “new imaginaries.”
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: New Hampshire voters pick 2026 midterm candidates
stories.description: A late surge by a progressive challenger has injected drama into New Hampshire's Democratic Senate primary on Tuesday, threatening to complicate US Representative Chris Pappas' path to nomination. In one of the last states holding primaries in 2026, New Hampshire voters will also choose nominees in a Republican Senate primary and in primaries for two US House seats, just eight weeks before the November 3 general election when control of Congress is at stake. France 24's Fraser Jackson has the latest.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 'The age of cultural resurgence': Africa's mother tongues finding new life
stories.description: Across the African continent, indigenous languages, once marginalised under colonial rule, are seeing renewed interest from younger generations, especially in the diaspora. Modern technology is providing them with new ways to reconnect with their heritage and older generations of their families. Clemence Waller reports.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Who is Sarah Khalifa, the Egyptian TV presenter sentenced to death?
stories.description: An Egyptian court has sentenced a well-known television presenter and 11 others to death for manufacturing and trafficking narcotics in a sprawling drugs case. The presenter, Sarah Khalifa, 39, is best known for her program "Mission Impossible", which dealt with issues concerning security and crime.
stories.subject: Health

stories.title: UK, France and ten other countries to sanction trade from Israeli settlements
stories.description: Twelve countries including Britain, Canada and France Tuesday said they would slap sanctions on trade with Israeli settlements in the West Bank, after increasing attacks by Israeli settlers against Palestinian villages in the occupied territory. British Foreign Minister Ed ​Miliband said Britain ‌could no longer simply "call out" injustice and suffering, but told the House of Commons that the country now had ⁠to "act" to oppose the expansion of settlements.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 'Be kind with yourself': US expat Robin Allison Davis on surviving cancer in Paris
stories.description: An American woman who moved to Paris and soon afterwards was twice diagnosed with breast cancer has spoken to FRANCE 24 about how she managed to get through the trauma. The paperback version of Robin Allison Davis's book "Surviving Paris: A Memoir of Healing in the City of Light" has just come out. The reviews say it's full of sorrow, laughter and some unforgettable cringeworthy moments. Davis told us the only way to survive in her situation was to be kind to herself, admitting that she did a lot of writing and crying at the same time. She spoke to us in Perspective.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Canada's counter-tariffs take effect as trade war with US heats up
stories.description: Canada's retaliatory tariffs on billions of dollars in US products took effect Tuesday, as a trade war between the North American neighbors heats up. On Monday, Trump had threatened to block sales of Canada's Bombardier Aviation in the United States, unless the Quebec-based plane maker moves manufacturing to the US.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: As Houthis attack Saudi Arabia, is Iran war escalating into regional conflict?
stories.description: Saudi Arabia on Tuesday threatened to hit back after a wave of missiles from Yemen's Houthis set oil facilities ablaze and wounded dozens, the Iran-backed rebels' heaviest attack in years. It comes after a four-year truce collapsed in July, months into the Middle East war between the United States and Iran. France 24's Rochelle Ferguson Bouyahi provides analysis.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Ukraine decries 'horrific' Russian attack shortly after US envoys leave
stories.description: Ukraine criticised Russia on Tuesday for launching a major missile and drone attack that killed at least two people shortly after a weekend visit by US envoys to both countries' capitals, where they tried to restart stalled talks on ending the war.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Who are the Hindu group cited in Eiffel Tower staff walk out?
stories.description: The Eiffel Tower reopened on Tuesday after staff walked out over the removal of women colleagues during a visit by a Hindu religious group. The Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha (BAPS) spiritual movement later apologised for "any pain or inconvenience caused" by the incident. France 24’s Delano D’Souza takes a closer look.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Russia pounds Kyiv, ending three-day halt for US talks
stories.description: Russian missiles and drones pounded Kyiv overnight, killing two people and sending smoke billowing above the Ukrainian capital, ending Moscow's temporary halt to strikes on the city.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: In Ukraine, teens try to heal from trauma of war at summer camp
stories.description: The psychological impact on the Ukrainian population of nearly five years of full-scale Russian onslaught is hard to overstate. Children and teenagers are particularly at risk of trauma. With support from foreign philanthropists, one Ukrainian NGO is trying to help at least a few teenagers cope better, via summer camps that mix therapy and fun. Our correspondent Gulliver Cragg reports.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Paris looks to profit as Céline Dion fans flock to French capital
stories.description: Céline Dion’s hotly anticipated return to the stage is scheduled for this Saturday in Paris - the first of more than 16 concerts in the French capital in September and October. The shows mark a major milestone for 58-year-old Dion after years away from touring due to the rare neurological disorder. A total of 500,000 spectators are expected in Paris - a huge windfall for the economy, especially for the hotel, restaurant, and transport industries.
stories.subject: Business

stories.title: France, South Korea pledge 1 billion euros to support cinema amid AI threat
stories.description: Hollywood star George Clooney and executives from US studios such as Sony Pictures and Disney were among the 200 guests that gathered in the south of France for a summit on the future of cinema on Monday. As part of the initiative, co-hosts France and south Korea have pledged 1 billion euros to safeguard against threats to the industry, particularly from AI.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: 'Pheromone maxxing': Men avoid showers before dates to boost attraction
stories.description: PRESS REVIEW – Tuesday, September 8: Papers discuss UK sanctions on Israeli settlements in the West Bank. Also, could AI change what it means to be human? Finally, "pheromone maxxing" is in; showers are out.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Nepal’s Gen Z protests one year on
stories.description: September 8 marks a year since a Gen Z-led violent revolt against corruption in Nepal forced the then prime minister to resign. The protests were triggered when government tried to suspend many prominent social media platforms for failing to comply with new Nepalese A year on, and as the country still grapples with the devastation caused by deadly floods, Morgan Ayre looks back at how Nepal got to this point and the challenges that lie ahead.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: ‘Truly terrifying’: AfD election win sparks protests across Germany
stories.description: The victory of the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) in Sunday's state election in Saxony-Anhalt sparked protests across Germany on Monday, as demonstrators called for a united front against the hardline anti-immigrant party. Some protesters call for the party, some of whose members have praised the Nazis, to be banned, but others say AfD's success is a result of a failure of mainstream political parties.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: London pub celebrates Bayeux Tapestry loan with ‘Beer Tapestry’
stories.description: Britons will finally get the chance to view the Bayeux Tapestry on home soil this week, as the 11th century work goes on display at the British Museum. And the exhibition has inspired a copycat tapestry, available to view for thirsty visitors seeking refreshment at a pub across the street.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: UAE leader warned Netanyahu of Hamas attack days before October 7, says report
stories.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu faced strong backlash from opposition leaders on Tuesday after a report published by Haaretz newspaper said UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan warned Netanyahu that Hamas was planning a major operation days before the attacks on October 7. The report alleges that Netanyahu failed to inform security chiefs.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: French legionnaire escapes Colombian captors, makes four-day trek to freedom
stories.description: A Colombian soldier in the French Foreign Legion who was taken hostage by guerrillas in Colombia escaped his captors after a four-day trek on foot through rebel-held territory. Jose Olger Melo Charry was taken hostage on August 6 by a dissident faction of the now-defunct FARC guerrilla group while he was traveling on a highway in Colombia's southwest.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: What is Germany's political 'firewall' and can it keep out the AfD?
stories.description: Alternative for Germany, or AfD, has established itself as a significant political force in the 13 years since its founding, but it has never been part of any state or federal government. That’s a result of what is often called a “firewall” against cooperation with the anti-immigrant, far-right party. France 24's Philip Turle explains.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: Russia pounds Kyiv after pause for visit of US envoys
stories.description: Russia pummelled Kyiv with drones and missiles early on Tuesday, resuming its air attacks after a brief halt for the visit of US peace negotiators, killing two people and triggering fires across the Ukrainian capital. France 24’s correspondent in Kyiv Emmanuelle Chaze has the latest.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Trump threatens ban on Bombardier as Canada's retaliatory tariffs kick in
stories.description: Canada's retaliatory tariffs of up to 50 percent on approximately $19.8 billion worth of US goods came into effect this Tuesday, further escalating the trade war between the two neighbours. At the same time, US President Donald Trump is threatening to ban sales of all Bombardier aircraft in the US, in spite of the Canadian company's deep web of US suppliers. Also in this edition: Iran raises the price of gasoline and French startup Mistral AI is now valued at €21 billion.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Houthi attacks disrupt Saudi oil facilities and wound more than 70
stories.description: Attacks on Saudi Arabia Tuesday claimed by Yemen's Houthis wounded more than 70 people and ignited fires at several oil facilities and utilities in the kingdom's southern region, authorities said, in a major escalation in the renewed conflict between an important US ally and the Iranian-backed rebels.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Thieves steal works of art worth 9 million euros from France's Renoir museum
stories.description: Two thieves on Tuesday broke into the Renoir Museum in the town of Cagnes-sur-Mer in southern France and stole "four works of art", dropping one as they fled, according to the local mayor. Officials estimated the value of the stolen works at 9 million euros.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: French AI startup Mistral valued at over 21 billion euros after latest funding
stories.description: French AI company Mistral announced Tuesday that it had raised three billion euros ($3.5 billion) in what it described as the largest-ever European tech fundraising, valuing the startup at over 21 billion euros. While still an upstart compared to the AI giants OpenAI or Anthropic, Mistral says it is carving a niche by offering models that companies can run themselves with their own data.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Nepal rescuers race to free dozens trapped in hydropower tunnels
stories.description: Authorities in Nepal on Tuesday said that rescuers are focusing on three hydropower project tunnels where they believe dozens of workers could be trapped. The announcement came two weeks after ​a devastating ‌flood killed that hundreds and left thousands missing in the Himalayan country and in ⁠neighbouring China's Tibet region.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Rubio kicks off tour in Latin America as US vies for regional influence
stories.description: United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Tuesday arrived in Colombia following the recent election of hard-right lawyer and US ally President Abelardo de la Espriella, and a string of right-wing electoral victories across Latin America. Colombia is the first stop on a tour designed to bolster pro-US leaders and cement influence over the continent.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 🔴 Live: At least two killed in Kyiv as Russia renews strikes after three-day pause
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Before Champions League, Kylian Mbappé campaigns for Ballon d'Or
stories.description: As the Champions League resumes, Real Madrid are hosting Inter Milan. Speaking at a press conference, Kylian Mbappé believes he has every chance of winning the Ballon d’Or.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Canada's counter-tariffs take effect on several US goods as trade war reignites
stories.description: Canada's counter-tariffs on billions of dollars in US products took effect Tuesday, as a trade war between the two countries heated up. Ottawa's pushback comes weeks after US President Donald Trump imposed 50-percent tariffs on a similar value of Canadian products, over what Washington deemed as "discriminatory treatment" against US alcohol, automobile and dairy industries.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Trump threatens to ban Canadian Bombardier jets from US market
stories.description: US President Donald Trump threatened on Monday to block sales of Canadian planemaker Bombardier in the United States unless it builds aircraft in the country, escalating trade tensions on the eve of Canadian retaliatory tariffs. Trump accused Canada of “unjust and unfair” trade practices but did not explain how a ban would work.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: Nearly 1.7 million deaths linked to second-hand smoke in 2023, study finds
stories.description: More than 2.7 billion people worldwide, including 767 million children, were exposed to second-hand smoke in 2023, contributing to nearly 1.7 million deaths, a Lancet study said on Tuesday. Researchers found second-hand smoke remained a major global health risk, with no safe level of exposure.
stories.subject: Science

stories.title: Eiffel Tower closed in row over women removed for Hindu group
stories.description: The Eiffel Tower was closed on Monday because of a strike by staff over the removal of female colleagues during a visit by a Hindu religious group, workers and management said. FRANCE 24's Monte Francis has more.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: EU says no place for 'glorification of war criminals' as Mladic buried
stories.description: The European Union on Monday denounced any "glorification" of convicted war criminal Ratko Mladic in Serbia, as thousands gathered in Belgrade for his funeral. FRANCE 24's James Vasina reports.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Israel intensifies South Lebanon strikes, killing 13 after weeks-long lull
stories.description: Israel launched a wave of airstrikes across southern Lebanon, killing 13 people, including women and children, Lebanon’s health ministry said on Monday, marking an escalation after weeks of relative calm. Israel said it would continue targeting Iran-backed Hezbollah over alleged ceasefire violations. Hezbollah has not commented on the strikes.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Volkswagen's Osnabrück plant to switch from cars to defence
stories.description: Crisis-hit Volkswagen has struck a preliminary deal to sell its Osnabrück plant in Lower Saxony to the state government and Israeli investor Aurelius Capital. From mid 2027, the iconic factory is expected to start producing equipment for Rafael Advanced Defence Systems, the company behind the Iron Dome missile defence system. But first, a look at the state of the German economy following far-right AfD's historic election win in Saxony-Anhalt.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Egyptian influencer's death penalty over drug charges
stories.description: In tonight's edition, a South African high court rejects a former defence minister's bid to have a corruption case against her dropped. Also, an Egyptian TV presenter is amongst a dozen people the court has sentenced to death on drug charges. And the very first Pan-African Architecture Biennale opened its doors on Monday in the Kenyan capital.
stories.subject: Health

stories.title: Only the beginning? German far-right's breakthrough shakes Europe to its core
stories.description: Not enough to win outright but enough to shake Germany and Europe to their core: the far-right Alterniv für Deutschland trouncing the ruling conservatives in the impoverished former East German region of Saxony-Anhalt. We’ll ask about the consequences of voting for an anti-immigrant, pro-Russian party that wants schools to teach less about the ills of Hitler and more the glory of Bismarck.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 'Polarised Brazil': Lula remains a ‘strong candidate’ despite the challenges of incumbency
stories.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome Andreza Aruska de Souza Santos, Director of King’s Brazil Institute at the School of Global Affairs, King’s College London and Associate Professor in Brazil and Latin American Studies. According to Aruska, Brazil’s approaching elections can be viewed through the following prism: macroeconomic performance and political confidence are moving on different tracks. While headline indicators may suggest an economy performing relatively well, she argues that many Brazilians experience a much harsher reality shaped by the cost of living and a volatile job market.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Tunisians tell the story of their summer of shortages
stories.description: Frequent water and power cuts, long queues for bottled water, poultry farms destroyed by the heat: these have been the scenes across Tunisia this summer as millions of people were affected by shortages in electricity and water. Our Observers say this is the result of years of underinvestment in infrastructure while the Tunisian president, for his part, blames "deliberate and planned acts of sabotage”.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: 'What we see right now is that Putin has zero interest in ending the war', Ukrainian MP Yasko says
stories.description: US envoy Steve Witkoff on Monday touted progress in weekend discussions with Ukraine and Russia, raising the prospect of reviving three-way peace talks to end Europe's deadliest conflict since World War II. Ukrainian MP Lisa Yasko says that "we don't trust these talks", describing the US envoys' flattery towards Russian President Vladimir Putin as "disgraceful".
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Israel warns of 'full-scale war' if Palestinian Authority launches Oct. 7-style attack
stories.description: Israel on Monday threatened a “full-scale war” against the Palestinian Authority if it believed the West Bank-based body was preparing an attack on Israeli forces or settlements resembling Hamas’s October 7, 2023 assault. The warning was denounced by Palestinian authorities as an attempt to fuel the conflict during the Israeli election season.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Eiffel Tower workers go on strike after female staff 'sidelined' for Hindu group's visit
stories.description: The Eiffel Tower was forced to close on Monday after staff went on strike to protest the “sidelining” and “replacement” of female employees during a recent visit by a Hindu delegation. The Paris landmark's operator said the group had requested that the private visit be organised in such a way as to limit “interactions with women”.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Avalanche kills at least 11 climbers in southern Russia
stories.description: ⁠At least ​11 people were killed and six ​others injured after an avalanche struck a group of climbers in Russia's ​southern Kabardino-Balkaria ‌Republic, local emergency services said. The ‌avalanche swept down Mount Mizhirgi, ⁠one of the highest peaks in Russia's North Caucasus.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Will AfD win in Germany boost France's far right?
stories.description: The Alternative for Germany (AfD) surged into first place in state elections in Saxony-Anhalt on Sunday, exit polls showed, putting a far-right party on the cusp of power at state level for the first time since World War Two. The result has garnered attention across Europe, not least in France where national elections next year could see far-right veteran Marine Le Pen become president.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Macron hosts summit to urge support for cinema amid impact of AI, streaming
stories.description: French President Emmanuel Macron on Monday called for stronger international efforts to protect cinema from the disruptive impact of artificial intelligence and streaming platforms while hosting more than 200 industry figures at the Lumière Summit in southern France.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon kill 11
stories.description: Israeli strikes ⁠on a ​southern Lebanese town early on Monday killed at least 11 people including two children ​and two medics, Lebanon's state news agency said. Israel has intensified its bombardment of south Lebanon in recent days despite a June ceasefire that was meant ​to halt fighting ‌between the Israeli military and Lebanese armed ⁠group Hezbollah.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Céline Dion and Jay-Z bring their hits to Paris
stories.description: In this edition of our arts24 music show, Jennifer Ben Brahim brings us a roundup of some of the week's most anticipated Paris concerts. From Céline Dion kicking off her 16 sold-out shows at La Défense Arena, to American rapper Jay-Z celebrating his 30-year career at the Stade de France, we've got you covered.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: What now for Germany's Merz after AfD win?
stories.description: The far-right AfD's triumph in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt marks a defeat for German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and sends a warning to other European leaders battling the same mixture of slow growth and disillusion with mainstream politics. In an increasingly polarized political system, Merz, whose personal approval ratings have sunk ‌to record lows, was one of the main targets of voter ire over the cost of living, pensions and economic insecurity. France 24’s Philip Turle takes a look at what the AfD’s victory means for the German leader and for Europe.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Saxony-Anhalt poll: 'A huge blow for the CDU, but also a huge win for the AfD'
stories.description: Carys Garland is pleased to welcome Markus Ziener, Visiting Senior Fellow at the German Marshall Fund. He interprets the AfD’s breakthrough in Saxony-Anhalt as a potentially historic turning point in post-war German politics. For Ziener, the significance lies not only in the scale of the far right’s electoral success, but also in the constituency behind it: many AfD voters, he argues, were previously politically disengaged rather than simply defecting from established parties. This complicates conventional explanations of the result as a straightforward transfer of support from the CDU to the AfD and raises a deeper question about the political expectations of a newly mobilised electorate.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: How far-right AfD breakthrough may ‘cause absolute chaos’ in Germany
stories.description: Germany’s Alternative for Germany (AfD) came out well ahead in Sunday’s regional elections in the state of Saxony-Anhalt, becoming the first far-right party to come close to gaining power at the regional level since World War II. The lead candidate of the party in the state, Ulrich Siegmund, said Monday that his party had already initiated talks towards building a governing majority.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Two children among dead in Israeli strikes on Lebanon
stories.description: Israeli airstrikes overnight killed 11 people in a south Lebanon village, including two infants, Lebanese state media said Monday, a day after separate raids left seven dead. France 24's Renée Davis in Beirut has the latest.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: REPLAY: 'Shocked' Merz speaks after far-right election victory
stories.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Monday he was "deeply shocked" after his centre-right party suffered a heavy loss in a state poll to the far-right AfD, but vowed to push on with reforms. Watch his press conference in full above.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: ‘Idiots and traitors’: World reacts to AfD’s election victory
stories.description: The Alternative for Germany (AfD) surged into first place in state elections in Saxony-Anhalt on Sunday. The result puts a far-right party within reach of power at the state level for the first time in the country since World War II. The outcome has European capitals taking notice, particularly in France where the campaign for next year's presidential elections has gotten underway.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Israeli rubble-clearing in Gaza could erase 'atrocity crimes' evidence: UN expert
stories.description: A UN expert warned Monday that large-scale rubble removal in parts of Gaza under Israeli control risked erasing traces of "atrocity crimes", and preventing the recovery and identification of human remains.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: UN rapporteur says Israeli rubble-clearing in Gaza could erase 'atrocity crimes' evidence
stories.description: The United Nations special rapporteur on Palestinian territories Francesca Albanese warned Monday that large-scale rubble removal in parts of Gaza under Israeli control could risk erasing "evidence relevant to the investigation of alleged international crimes". Israel's bombardment and ground offensive on Gaza has killed more than 73,000 Palestinians, according to Gaza's health ministry.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 'We’re all in crisis': Populist far-right 'trend' sweeping across Europe
stories.description: Annette Young is pleased to welcome our international affairs editor, Philip Turle, and Sylvie Bermann, France's first female ambassador to three member countries of the United Nations Security Council: China, the United Kingdom and Russia. The AfD’s breakthrough in Saxony-Anhalt should be understood, according to Sylvie Bermann, as part of a wider transformation of European politics rather than as an isolated German electoral shock. Brexit and Donald Trump’s victories helped normalise political positions previously regarded as outside the governing mainstream, while successive economic and geopolitical crises have weakened confidence in established parties.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Driverless taxi services are rolling out fast across the world
stories.description: From Austin to London, the current robotaxi boom is raising hard questions about safety and jobs. We take a closer look in this edition of Tech 24.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Who could form a coalition with Germany's AfD after election victory?
stories.description: Germany's far-right AfD won a landslide victory in a key regional election Sunday in the ex-communist east, a result seen as a stinging rebuke for Chancellor Friedrich Merz, but looked set to miss out on an absolute majority to govern alone. The big question now is who, if anyone, will be willing to form a coalition with the party, says France 24's correspondent Nick Holdsworth.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: French wine yields drop to new historic low after searing summer heat
stories.description: French wine production is expected to suffer its worst harvest in some 70 years with the agriculture ministry on Monday forecasting a 6 percent drop in output after a summer of scorching temperatures, heatwaves and drought. France last week announced more than €1 billion in emergency support for farmers.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: 'This might be the year': Mbappé embraces Ballon d'Or talk after World Cup exploits
stories.description: Real Madrid star Kylian Mbappé played up his chances of the winning the Ballon d'Or this year after scoring 10 goals at the recent World Cup to become the tournament's all-time leading scorer. Nominees for the prestigious award will be unveiled on Tuesday.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Five dead after Amazon cargo plane overshoots runway in Miami
stories.description: At least five people died when an Amazon Prime Air cargo flight overran a runway and crashed while landing at Miami International ​Airport on Sunday, local ‌officials said.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Lebanon president calls for US help after deadly Israeli strikes
stories.description: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun has urged Washington and the international community to help stop Israeli attacks, with strikes on the south of the country killing at least 11 people on Sunday despite a truce and a framework deal aimed at halting the violence.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Segregated schools and citizen ‘watch groups’: the AfD’s plans for Saxony-Anhalt
stories.description: The Alternative for Germany (AfD) surged into first place in state elections in Saxony-Anhalt on Sunday, exit polls showed, putting a far-right party within reach of power at the state level for the first time since World War Two. So who are the AfD, and what could it mean for voters in the state? Rachael Griffiths has more.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 'Jubilation and pain': German far right marches to victory in key state election
stories.description: PRESS REVIEW – Monday, September 7: The far right marches to victory in a German state election: what does this mean for the future of Germany and Europe at large? Also: the Daily Telegraph publishes an exclusive interview with the sons of former Pakistani PM Imran Khan about his imprisonment conditions in Pakistan. Plus the US Open descends into chaos after influencers, weed and disruptions stir controversy.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Jamaica’s legal approach: Were forced transportation & African enslavement lawful under English law?
stories.description: Eve Irvine is pleased to welcome Jamaica’s Minister of Culture, Gender, Entertainment and Sport, Olivia Grange. According to Grange, the country’s reparations initiative attempts to shift the debate over British slavery from the terrain of political discretion to that of legal accountability. Was the capture, transportation and chattel enslavement of Africans in Jamaica ever lawful? Jamaica’s petition therefore asks King Charles III, in his capacity as King of Jamaica, to refer three questions to the Privy Council concerning English law, international law and Britain’s possible obligation to provide a reparatory remedy.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Far-right AfD wins crushing victory in German state election
stories.description: The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) surged into first place in state elections in Saxony-Anhalt on Sunday, exit polls showed, putting it within reach of power at the state level for the first time since World War Two, though falling just short of an overall majority.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Why are tourists flocking to French pharmacies?
stories.description: After visiting the monuments and department stores, for some tourists in France, it’s off to the pharmacy. More and more foreign tourists are taking advantage of their stay to stock up on cosmetic products, sold in many pharmacies in France, which are known to be less expensive and very popular on social media.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: German startup carries out Europe's first commercial space launch
stories.description: German startup Isar Aerospace successfully launched its Spectrum rocket into orbit from Norway on Saturday night, marking the first ever such launch by a commercial entity from European soil. European firms are racing to make up ground in the lucrative launch industry, currently dominated by America's SpaceX.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: German startup notches Europe's first successful private orbital launch
stories.description: German startup Isar Aerospace becomes the first company to achieve a successful private orbital space launch. But first: Germany's far-right AfD party scores a big electoral victory, pushed along in part by the country's structural economic crisis and its fiscal policies.
stories.subject: Science

stories.title: Nepal holds a day of mourning as rescuers continue search for flood missing
stories.description: Grief-stricken Nepalis entered the traditional Hindu last day of mourning on Monday for the hundreds who died in the catastrophic flood along the country's border with China even as the government kept search operations going ​after four ‌miracle rescues in recent days.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Germany seeks to dismiss Nicaragua's Gaza genocide case at top UN court
stories.description: Germany is set to ask the International Court of Justice on Monday to dismiss a case accusing Berlin of "facilitating genocide" in Gaza by supporting Israel after the deadly October 7, 2023 attacks by Hamas militants. The details of the case, filed by Nicaragua in 2024, have not yet been made public.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Yemen govt forces, Houthi rebels battle for control of Red Sea gateway
stories.description: Military sources in Yemen say more than 140 combatants were killed in fighting between its government and Houthi rebels in the southwest of the country over the weekend. Days-long clashes have erupted in the country over the control of a gateway to the Red Sea, marking the deadliest fighting in the Arabian Peninsula country since a 2022 ceasefire between the two sides collapsed in July.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Signs of progress after US envoys Witkoff and Kushner hold talks in Ukraine?
stories.description: US peace envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff heralded new momentum in peace talks after meeting Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy in Kyiv on Sunday as the Trump administration renewed its push to end Russia's four-and-a-half-year war in Ukraine. But while there maybe some tentative signs that the proposals from the US team are more to Ukraine’s liking than those previously put forward, what Moscow thinks is still unclear, says France 24’s Oliver Farry.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Five dead after Amazon cargo plane crashes in Miami airport
stories.description: At least five people were killed when an Amazon cargo plane overshot a runway after it landed Sunday at Miami International Airport, officials said. Prime Air ⁠Flight 7598 overran the airport's diagonal runway shortly before 2 p.m. EDT (1800 GMT) and struck multiple vehicles on the ground, officials said during a news conference on ‌Sunday afternoon.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Germany: 'Hard to say' if AfD win the result of protest vote
stories.description: The Alternative for Germany (AfD) surged into first place in state elections in Saxony-Anhalt on Sunday, exit polls showed, putting a far-right party within reach of power at the state level for the first time since World War Two. However, France 24’s correspondent in Berlin, Nick Holdsworth, says it is “hard to say” if the victory is more the result of dissatisfaction with Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s governing conservatives, or an explicit endorsement of the AfD.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Two far-right activists go on trial in Paris over 2022 killing of Argentine rugby star Aramburu
stories.description: Two-far activists go on trial in Paris on Monday over the shooting of Argentine rugby star Federico Martin Aramburu. Loik Le Priol and Romain Bouvier have been charged with murder and attempted murder respectively, and risk up to life in jail if they are found guilty.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: 🔴 Germany: Victory of far-right AfD in state election 'very worrying', says Polish FM
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Ligue 1: Paris FC and Sinayoko beat Marseille and climb to 2nd
stories.description: Paris FC beat Olympique de Marseille 3–2 at the Vélodrome thanks to a hat-trick from Lassine Sinayoko. Paris FC sit second but OM remain stuck in 10th place in the table.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Wildfires, heatwaves threaten global air quality and health, UN warns
stories.description: Wildfires and heatwaves are threatening global efforts to improve air quality and protect human health, the World Meteorological Organisation said on Monday. The UN agency warned that increasingly severe fires are raising exposure to toxic PM2.5 pollution, even as regulations have reduced industrial and transport emissions in Europe and North America.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Middle East Live: Israel army orders evacuation of zone in south Lebanon ahead of strikes
stories.description: The Israeli army demanded early Monday that residents of Deir Zahrani in southern Lebanon leave a specific zone ahead of strikes against Iran-backed Hezbollah. Hezbollah's Al-Manar television channel later reported Israeli airstrikes on Deir Zahrani. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: US envoys bring ‘more effective’ Ukraine peace proposals to Kyiv, official says
stories.description: US envoys brought new, “more effective” proposals to Kyiv aimed at ending the war with Russia, a senior Ukrainian presidential official said on Sunday. President Volodymyr Zelensky and US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner described talks positively but announced no breakthrough, as Zelensky warned fighting could continue into winter.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: EU to boost Greenland investment amid Trump annexation claims
stories.description: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen is expected to announce increased EU investment in Greenland on Monday, including in critical minerals, satellite communications and renewable energy. Her two-day visit signals support for Greenland and Denmark amid US President Donald Trump’s push for American control of the Arctic territory.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: Amazon cargo plane crashes at Miami airport, killing at least five
stories.description: At least five people were killed and five injured after an Amazon cargo plane overshot the runway at Miami International Airport on Sunday and crashed into several vehicles, officials said. Miami Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz said there was “no apparent threat to public safety” following the crash.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: "Ready to talk": German far-right celebrates victory
stories.description: “Everything is possible” is the election campaign slogan of the far-right Alternative for Germany, the leader in Saxony-Anhalt, where the polls have just closed. It talks of a seminal moment for the country. Ulrich Siegmund, who has been polling in pole position to become the state leader, knows he has history in his grasp.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 🔴Germany’s far-right AfD landslide winner in key Saxony-Anhalt vote, early results suggest
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Germany’s far-right AfD landslide winner in key Saxony-Anhalt vote, early results suggest
stories.description: Germany’s far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party headed towards a landslide victory in state ​elections in Saxony-Anhalt on Sunday, with 44.5 percent of the vote, early results showed.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Deauville Film Festival: What’s your favourite American film?
stories.description: The United States ranks second in the world in terms of the number of films produced. It produces between 500 and 700 films every year, which is just behind India. The Deauville Film Festival, with its stars, premieres and awards, aims to showcase the very best of what’s being made across the Atlantic. But on the other side of the screen, moviegoers also have their say. What’s your favourite American film? Is it one that shaped your childhood, or a recent discovery? Our reporter Gaëlle Fonseca hit the streets of Deauville to ask that very question.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Germany: What could change in Saxony-Anhalt if the AfD wins?
stories.description: Voting began in the eastern German state of Saxony-Anhalt on Sunday in a closely watched election. Recent surveys place the AfD at just over 40%, followed by Merz's Christian Democrats (CDU) at 23%. If the AfD wins, "one of the main things they want to change is the education system. They say they want to reset education," our journalist Shirli Stibon explains.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Under-fire FIFA boss Infantino to seek re-election despite calls to resign
stories.description: FIFA President Gianni Infantino plans to seek his fourth and final term in next year’s election, despite the outrage sparked by his now-shelved plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors. “Nothing has changed,” a spokesman for football’s governing body confirmed on Sunday, referring to an announcement Infantino made back in April.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: The week in pictures: Nepal rescue operations, World Nomad Games and Russian strikes on Kyiv
stories.description: From the desperate search for workers trapped in the hydropower tunnels buried by the catastrophic flooding in Nepal to crowds of women mourning the victims of a US bombardment of a wedding in southern Iran, FRANCE 24 looks back at the week's most striking pictures.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Germany: AfD's Ulrich Siegmund eyes outright majority
stories.description: Under its 35-year-old lead ​candidate Ulrich Siegmund, the ‌AfD has polled above 40% for months and has a realistic shot at winning an absolute majority if several smaller parties fail ⁠to clear Germany's 5% hurdle to enter parliament.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Ukraine-Russia talks: What are the US objectives?
stories.description: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Kyiv on Sunday in their first official visit to Ukraine as part of a renewed push for peace, more than 4½ years after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. We discuss this topic with our guest, John E. Herbst, director of the Eurasia Center at the Atlantic Council.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Egyptian TV presenter Sarah Khalifa sentenced to death in drug case
stories.description: Sarah Khalifa, a well-known Egyptian TV presenter, has been sentenced to death for her involvement in a drug ring, state media reported over the weekend. Eleven others were also convicted in the case and handed a death sentence. Khalifa is best known for her program “Mission Impossible”.
stories.subject: Health

stories.title: AI: The future of smart households?
stories.description: Could artificial intelligence soon be running our households? Beyond our smartphones, AI is now powering everything from fridges to lawnmowers. The International Household Appliances Fair in Berlin gives us a glimpse into what's next.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Germany: Why is the AfD so popular in Saxony-Anhalt?
stories.description: Voting began in the eastern German state of Saxony-Anhalt on Sunday in a closely watched election that could see the Alternative for Germany (AfD) become the first far-right party to lead a state government since World War II. We discuss this with our guest, Hans Stark, professor of German studies at Sorbonne University.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Indonesia's Anak Krakatau eruption halts flights, schools, fishing
stories.description: An eruption of Indonesia's Mount Anak Krakatau caused six airports to suspend flight operations on Sunday, affecting hundreds of flights at Jakarta's main airport, after some school activities and fishing were halted.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Commemoration held for late Bosnian Serb war criminal Ratko Mladic
stories.description: A commemoration was held Saturday in Belgrade for war criminal Ratko Mladic two days ahead of his burial, attended by dozens of former military personnel, family members and officials.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Germany's far-right AfD clear frontrunner in eastern state vote
stories.description: German voters headed to the polls on Sunday for a key regional election in the ex-communist east where the far-right, anti-immigrant, Moscow- and Trump-friendly AfD is expected to secure an easy majority. Our correspondent Nick Holdsworth tells us more.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Ethan Hawke receives the Deauville Talent Award
stories.description: Known for starring in Dead Poets Society, the Before trilogy and Boyhood, Hollywood legend Ethan Hawke receives the #Deauville #Talent #Award in recognition of his career spanning nearly 40 years. He also plays the lead role in The Weight, screened at the Opening Ceremony of the 52nd Deauville #American #Film #Festival and due to be released in theaters on September 16. Our reporter Gaëlle Fonseca spoke to him on the red carpet.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: US Army Secretary Dan Driscoll quits: "What we've seen is almost a factional clash"
stories.description: Amid the US conflict with Iran, Democrats and some Republicans are warning of a leadership void at the top of the US military. That's after the resignation this week of the Army's top civilian official, Army Secretary Dan Driscoll, amid widespread reports of tensions with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Our guest, Walter Ladwig, associate professor of international relations at King's College London, tells us more.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 🔴 Trump's envoys Witkoff and Kushner arrive in Kyiv after 'substantive' talks with Putin
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Iran claims strike on US ship in Strait of Hormuz as fighting escalates
stories.description: Iran said Sunday it struck an unmanned U.S. vessel trying to enter the Strait of Hormuz, the latest salvo in a new flare-up of fighting between the two countries.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Nepal floods: Search operations enter 12th day
stories.description: Nepali rescuers faced challenging conditions on Sunday as search operations following catastrophic floods entered their 12th day, buoyed by the extraordinary rescue of four survivors. The disaster has also affected infrastructure and roads. Our correspondent Shahzaib Wahlah tells us more.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Germany's far-right AfD clear frontrunner in eastern state vote
stories.description: German voters headed to the polls Sunday for a crucial regional election in the ex-communist east where the far-right, anti-immigration and Moscow-friendly AfD is expected to win easily.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill four in Lebanon after alleged Hezbollah drone launch
stories.description: Israeli air strikes on southern Lebanon Sunday killed four people, two of them women, the country's health ministry said. Israel's military said that the strikes were a response to an alleged Hezbollah drone launch targeting troops in the Israeli-occupied "security zone" in the country's south.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Eight airports in Indonesia suspend operations after volcanic eruption
stories.description: Eight airports in Indonesia, including Jakarta's main international airport, suspended operations Sunday after the erupting Anak Krakatoa volcano spewed clouds of ash across the archipelago. Geologists said that the latest series of eruptions does not have the potential to trigger a tsunami at this time.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: 'A bad sign': US envoys head to Kyiv after three-hour talks with Putin
stories.description: As US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner head to Kyiv following what the White House described as "substantive" talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin, FRANCE 24 correspondent Gulliver Cragg talks about what he describes as a climate of scepticism in Ukraine that these latest negotiations could bring a long-awaited breakthrough.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Germany's far-right AfD eyes historic state victory in Saxony-Anhalt election
stories.description: Germany's anti-immigrant Alternative for Germany party is aiming to become the first far-right party to take power at a state level since World War II as voters in the eastern German state of Saxony-Anhalt head to the polls Sunday. However, a failure to secure an absolute majority may see the politically isolated party struggle to form a government.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Witkoff: Putin’s Messenger?
stories.description: What did Steve Witkoff know about Russia when he was first sent to see President Putin in February last year?
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: The closely-watched Lindsay Clancy trial ends with one last dramatic moment
stories.description: The closely watched case of the Massachusetts mother who killed her three young children was on the verge of being declared a mistrial Friday — but there was still one more dramatic moment to come.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: 'Wallace & Gromit' creators turn 50 with spook-tacular Shaun yarn
stories.description: Crochet hook in hand, the animator slightly raises the eyelid of a clay model sheep in a filmmaking technique as old as cinema, perfected over five decades by Aardman Animations.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: UN approves resolution in support of map that shows Africa's true size
stories.description: The United Nations on ‌Friday voted for a shift away from the 16th-century Mercator global map towards one more accurately reflecting countries' true size, a resolution sponsored by African states to counter perceptions that the continent is peripheral.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: ‘Rain man’ to the rescue? France’s ex-president Hollande plots unlikely comeback
stories.description: Once so deeply unpopular he had to give up running for a second term in office, former French president François Hollande has slipped back into the conversation ahead of next year’s Élysée Palace race, hoping voters put off by squabbling candidates will come to see him as a safe – if unexciting – pair of hands after a decade of Emmanuel Macron’s ‘disruptive’ presidency.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Chinese national rescued from Nepal tunnel 10 days after flash flood
stories.description: A Chinese national was pulled alive from a tunnel in Nepal on Saturday, authorities said, 10 ‌days after a wall of ice, rock and mud tore through a Himalayan valley, killing more than 1,300 people.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: War in Ukraine: Putin, Zelensky order pause in strikes
stories.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Saturday ordered a 72-hour pause in strikes on Kyiv as US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Moscow.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: US envoys Witkoff, Kushner arrive in Moscow for talks on peace in Ukraine
stories.description: US special representatives Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner landed in Moscow on Saturday for talks on how to end the ‌war in Ukraine, where they were met by Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev. Our guest Jamie Smith-Maillet tells us more.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 'Culture of fear within US Defence Department: Slow leakage of dissent against the administration'
stories.description: Catherine Viette is pleased to welcome Dafydd Townley, Senior Teaching Fellow in International Security at the University of Portsmouth. He argues that the turmoil surrounding Pete Hegseth points to a problem much deeper than personnel disputes at the Pentagon: The removal and marginalization of experienced officials, the weakening of professional military education, and the prioritization of political loyalty risk changing the institutional culture through which the US military evaluates strategy and challenges political authority.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Paris hosts African Diaspora International Film Festival
stories.description: This weekend, Paris is hosting the 16th edition of FIFDA, the African Diaspora International Film Festival. From September 4 to 6, 15 films from 13 countries will be screened, spanning fiction and non-fiction, as well as feature-length and short films. The festival provides a space to explore how contemporary societies face and overcome wounds from the past, while giving a voice to members of African diasporas. Guest Lawrence Cole, co-executive producer of "Shadow of Greed", and Diarah N'Daw-Spech, FIFDA co-founder and co-director.
stories.subject: Science

stories.title: Uber announces immediate withdrawal from Nigeria and Uganda
stories.description: Uber has announced its immediate withdrawal from Nigeria and Uganda. The decision comes amid a global restructuring, but mainly as Uber has lost significant ground to its competitors in both countries.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: UN experts urge Sudan-wide arms embargo
stories.description: A weapons embargo must be extended to the whole of Sudan, and it must be enforced. That is, in essence, the conclusion of a UN experts' report presented to the Human Rights Council. The report also points to the responsibility of foreign entities in a conflict that has now been raging for more than three years. Our correspondent Bastien Renouil tells us more.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Nepal: Two more people rescued alive
stories.description: Rescuers in Nepal pulled out a Chinese man and a woman in separate operations Saturday, 10 days after devastating floods hit the country, as teams continued searching for thousands of missing people. Our correspondent Shahzaib Wahlah tells us more.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Witkoff and Kushner are in Moscow in a new push for peace between Russia and Ukraine
stories.description: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Moscow on Saturday to try to revive a stalled push to end Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Russian state news outlets reported. Our correspondent Gulliver Cragg tells us more.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: France: Emmanuel Macron unveils new disability strategy
stories.description: French President Emmanuel Macron delivered the closing speech at the national conference on disability. It is an event the government holds every three years. It aims to set or guide policies. Macron made disability one of the priorities of his first five-year term. Since 2017, the government has implemented a number of measures to better integrate people with disabilities into society. According to official figures, between 5.7 and 18.2 million people aged five and older in France have a disability. We discuss this with our guest, Dr. Johny Daniel, associate professor at the School of Education at Durham University.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Presidential campaigning kicks off in France ahead of 2027 elections
stories.description: On April 18th and May 2nd next year - France will be voting to elect a new president to replace Emmanuel Macron. The country's latest opinion polls predict a victory for Marine le Pen of the Far-right National Rally. Although the election is still over seven months away, many potential candidates have already thrown their hats into the ring. But do any of them stand a chance of beating the far right? Our guest Eleanor Beardsley from National Public Radio answers that question.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Two Nepal rescues revive hopes 10 days after flood
stories.description: Rescuers in Nepal pulled alive on Saturday a Chinese national from a tunnel and a local woman from her partially submerged home, as emergency response teams searched with renewed vigour for thousands missing since catastrophic flooding 10 days ago. Our correspondent Shahzaib Wahlah tells us more.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: DR Congo: Ebola burial teams race against time
stories.description: In eastern DR Congo, Ebola burial teams are racing against time as the outbreak continues to spread.
